title: Protestants take justify forensically: absolve before God
source_text: XLI. Quod spectat ergo Protestantes, verbum justificare in hac quaestione sumunt sensu forensi, nec per justificari aliud intelligunt, quam a peccato absolvi, & infon-tem pronunciari. Hae vero voces coram Deo, ipsis idem sunt atque in districti Dei judicio, & secundum legis rigorem instituto. Itaque, quum negant nos per inhae-rentem justitiam coram Deo justificari, eorum mens est, neminem ratione sanctitatis & justitiae ullius quae in ipso reperiatur, & bonorum quae fecerit operum, posse in severo Dei judicio infontem pronunciari, & ab omni culpa absolvi: nec quemquam posse in Dei judicio damnationem effugere, & ad vitam aeternam, ut ea dignum acceptari, si justitiam & opera nostra Deus rigide examinet, nec ulla utatur erga nos clementia & misericordia.
pass_a_gloss: As for the Protestants, therefore, they take the word justify in this question in the forensic sense, and by being justified they understand nothing other than to be absolved from sin and pronounced innocent. But these words before God mean for them the same as in God's strict judgment instituted according to the rigor of the law. Therefore when they deny that we are justified before God by inherent righteousness, their mind is that no one, by reason of any holiness and righteousness found in him and of the good works he has done, can in God's severe judgment be pronounced innocent and absolved from all fault; nor can anyone in God's judgment escape damnation and be accepted as worthy of eternal life, if God rigidly examines our righteousness and works and uses no clemency and mercy toward us.
pass_b_english: Protestants take justify forensically: to be absolved and pronounced innocent before God under law's rigor.
Denying justification by inherent justice means no one's own holiness clears him if God examines without mercy.

choices.why: Protestant justificare = absolve before the Judge.
